title: Conformance Decision Rules: ISO 14253-1 & JCGM 106
subtitle: How measurement uncertainty shrinks the acceptance zone, trades off consumer risk against producer risk, and refuses to pass parts when uncertainty is missing (UEC-0).

standards.topic: Decision rules for verifying conformity or nonconformity with specifications
Guard banding, acceptance zones, specific and global consumer/producer risk

sections.heading: Why measured values near a tolerance limit are ambiguous
paragraphs: When a shaft diameter measures 10.045 mm against an upper specification limit of 10.050 mm, and expanded measurement uncertainty is U = 0.010 mm (u_std = 0.005 mm, k = 2), a substantial tail of the true-value probability distribution lies outside specification. A decision rule defines explicitly how that uncertainty governs the pass/fail verdict.

Simple acceptance (`dr:simple-acceptance@1`, shared risk) accepts whenever y lies inside [LSL, USL], exposing the customer to up to 50% specific consumer risk right at the limit. Guard-banded acceptance (`dr:guard-band(r=1)@1`) shrinks the acceptance zone inward by w = r * U, bounding consumer risk while increasing producer false-rejection risk. ISO 14253-1:2017 default (`dr:iso14253-1:2017/default@1`) requires at least 95% conformance probability to declare CONFORMS, marking the boundary band INDETERMINATE. That probability needs a probability distribution backed by a Monte Carlo check (JCGM 101:2008); the uncertainty in this lab is a bare u_std and k with no such check, so `fid-kdec` refuses with `NOT_DECIDABLE(pdf_unavailable)` rather than assume a normal distribution.

sections.heading: Fail-closed handling of UEC-0 (missing uncertainty)
paragraphs: `fid-kdec` never silently treats missing uncertainty as zero. When an uncertainty statement is UEC-0, every decision rule other than `dr:as-reported-by-source@1` returns `NOT_DECIDABLE(u_missing)` instead of fabricating a conforming verdict.

lab.instructions: Slide the measured value y across the tolerance band [9.950 mm, 10.050 mm], adjust standard uncertainty u_std, or switch decision rules (Simple Acceptance, ISO 14253-1 Default, Guard Band r=1, UEC-0) to watch fid-kdec compute outcomes, acceptance zones and global risk live in WebAssembly. Conformance probability and specific risk stay blank here: no Monte Carlo check backs the lab's uncertainty, and fid-kdec never assumes one.

presets.label: Near USL: Simple Acceptance (Shared Risk)
presets.description: Measured y = 10.045 mm vs. [9.950, 10.050] mm with u_std = 0.005 mm (U = 0.010 mm). Simple acceptance passes the part on the measured value alone, although U = 0.010 mm reaches past the upper limit; it does not weigh that uncertainty.

presets.label: Near USL: ISO 14253-1 Default (95% Conformance, Refused)
presets.description: The exact same measurement evaluated under ISO 14253-1:2017 default (p_min = 0.95). This rule needs a conformance probability, and no Monte Carlo check backs the lab's uncertainty, so fid-kdec refuses: NOT_DECIDABLE(pdf_unavailable). It never guesses p.

presets.label: Near USL: Strict Guard Band (r = 1.0)
presets.description: The exact same measurement under a full 1*U guard band (acceptance zone shrunk to [9.960, 10.040] mm): y = 10.045 mm lies outside the acceptance zone -> NONCONFORMS.

presets.label: Nominal Value with UEC-0 (Missing Uncertainty)
presets.description: Even dead-center at y = 10.000 mm, when uncertainty is UEC-0 (not evaluated), fid-kdec refuses to fabricate conformance and emits NOT_DECIDABLE(u_missing).
